Subject 4th District Street Cleaners' Union

Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by J Logan D.S.I

Efforts made to locate the persons responsible for
the re-establishment in the Settlement of the 4th District
Street Cleaners' Union at Lane 390, No.39 Chemulpo Road
have proved abortive. According to the principal tenant
of the house in question, two Chinese claiming to be
members of the Union, rented the downstairs front room at
a monthly rental of $12. They paid $5.00 on November 1
and promised to pay the balance later. However, these
two persons have not visited the office since November 5.
The principal tenant considers that as the rent has
not been paid, the lease has automatically expired, and he
is now advertising for a new tenant.
The board inscribed with the name of the Union,
which is affixed to the wall at the entrance to the alleyway,
has not yet been removed.

（批：Under no circumstances if still a Union was duly approved or authorized then Board should be removed.）

为查明负责在租界内 Chemulpo Road（音译）39号390弄重新设立第四区街道清洁夫工会的人员所作之努力已告失败。据该房屋的主要租户称，两名自称是工会成员的华人以每月12元的租金租下了楼下前间。他们于11月1日支付了5.00元，并承诺稍后支付余款。然而，自11月5日以来，这两人未曾到访办事处。主要租户认为，由于未支付租金，租赁契约已自动失效，他目前正在刊登广告寻找新租户。

Subject 4th District Street Cleaners' Union - Office

Made by U.S. McKeown Forwarded by [Signature]

On November 1, the office of the 4th District Street
Cleaners' Union was removed from Chapei to Lane 390, No.39
Chemulpo Road. The members of this union comprise street
cleaning and garbage coolies attached to the Antung Road
Depot of the P.W.D. This organization was formed in 1935
by a group of opportunists, and since its inauguration has
concentrated on exploiting the P.W.D. coolies by collecting
fees and conducting agitation against the P.W.D. Authorities
to justify its existence.

On June 17, Li Liang-ping (厲良斌), the secretary
of the union was informed by Mr. T. Robertson that enquiries
had elicited the information that the union had no official
standing with the Kuomintang Headquarters, and he was
instructed to wind up the affairs of the union and cease
activities in the Settlement. Subsequently the Kuomintang
Headquarters prepared a notification to be sent to the
People's Training Department ordering the immediate abolition
of the 4th District Street Cleaners' Union on the ground that
it was a highly undesirable organization, and it was later
reported that the permit issued to the union by the Social
Bureau had been withdrawn.

On June 25, 1936, the office of the union was removed
from Yangchow Road to 227-228 Ling Ka Tsu Loo (林家嘴路),
Hung Tseng (虹鎮), O.O.L. and while the office has been
located in Chinese territory, the union has ceased to be a
source of trouble to the Settlement Authorities.

制作人：U.S. McKeown 转呈人：[签名]

11月1日，第四区街道清洁夫工会的办事处从闸北迁至 Chemulpo Road（音译）39号390弄。该工会的成员包括隶属于工务局安通路堆栈的街道清洁夫和垃圾搬运苦力。该组织由一群投机分子于1935年成立，自成立以来，一直专注于通过收取费用并对抗工务局当局以证明其存在的合理性，从而剥削工务局的苦力。

Date May 16. 1936.

Subject 4th District Street Cleaners' Union.

Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by (签名)

The 4th District Street Cleaners' Union, Lane 310,
18 Yangchow Road, is making every effort to induce all P.W.D.
coolies in the Eastern District to join its ranks. Copies
of a manifesto issued by the Propaganda Department of the
Union and urging all coolies to support and join the union
were recently distributed in the Eastern District.

Tsang Loong-hai (莊龍海), ex-coolie and one of
the principal promoters of the union, has again been warned
to discontinue his activities. In reply he stated that he
was no longer interested in the affairs of the union and
had found employment elsewhere. However, information
indicates that he visits the union office daily, and has
still a controlling interest in the affairs of the union.

Two other committee members namely Woo Nying-foo
(胡良富) and Hsu Chi-zu (徐继儒), both P.W.D. coolies,
have also been warned against conducting agitation among the
coolies.

The primary cause of the unrest is the agitation
being conducted by the leading members of the union. It is
evident that the majority of the coolies are unwilling to
belong to the union and pay the monthly subscriptions, but
they are dominated by the leaders. Contributory causes
are the reports prevalent regarding reductions in staff,
and the introduction of new wheelbarrows which do not meet
with the approval of the coolies.

Made by D.S. White. Forwarded by

Sir,
At 2.30 p.m. on the 9-2-36 a meeting of about 70 P.W.D.
coolies was held at No. 18 San Ming Faung, Yangchow road to
discuss the attitude adopted by the P.W.D. authorities in
regard to P.W.D. coolies being members of the said Union, and
the dismissal of coolies.
The chairman of the meeting was a coolie named Woo Kyung
Foo (胡銀富) and ex P.W.D. coolie No. 673 named Tsong Loong
Hai (莊龍海) gave eloquent speeches concerning the methods of
certain P.W.D. foremen in respect of employing coolies. He
informed the gathering that these foremen deliberately dismiss
coolies so that they can engage new men from whom they extort
fees ranging from $20.00 to $50.00 according to the work that
is to be done. He also informed the gathering that should they,
through the methods used by these foremen, find themselves
without food etc, they must go to the homes of these foremen and
live on them.
At 5.30 p.m. the meeting broke up on the understanding that
it would be resumed at 2.30 p.m. on the 10-2-36.
Bureau of Social Affairs was represented by Yue Foong Foo
(俞方甫) who took no active part in the meeting.

Sir,
At about 6.00 a.m. on the 6-2-36 Mr. Vaslieff of the Antung Road P.W.D. Depot telephoned to the station and reported that there was some trouble between 2 of his coolies. From enquiries made the following was ascertained.
On the 1-2-36 coolie number 679 having died was struck off the strength and a new coolie named Koh Zau Ching (郭灶清) residing 514 Weinan Road was engaged and given the number of 679.
At about 5.40 a.m. even date when all the coolies mustered outside the office on Antung Road for duty No. 679 entered the office and informed Mr. Vaslieff that a coolie named Tsoong Loong Hai (章龍海) No. 673, residing country house off Chaoyang Road was going to assault him because he (679) had been given the job whereas he (673) wanted to employ a friend of his who happened to be ex-coolie No. 646 who had been dismissed for fighting. Mr. Vaslieff then called No. 673 into his office and asked him his version of the affair to which 673 replied that there was nothing wrong, Mr. Vaslieff then told both parties not to cause any trouble and to go to the respective jobs; something however must have aroused 673 because he suddenly became abusive resulting in him throwing his coolie's badge on Mr. Vaslieff's desk which meant that he was resigning. Mr. Vaslieff then informed him that he would report his resignation to his superiors at the Head-office. No. 673 then left the office and he was heard to say that he would give trouble to No. 679 when he was off duty.
At 11.30 a.m. No. 673 returned to the office and asked Mr. Vaslieff what the Head-office had done about his resignation

Superintendent of Cleansing & Watering,
P. W. D. S. M. C.

Sir,

Reference your instructions to investigate the cases of
I. R. Collection Coolies No. 615 and 647 of the Eastern Division
the following report is forwarded.

I. R. Collection Coolie No. 615 states:- He joined the
Council SERVICE three years ago, his age now is 21 years. He was
forced by I. R. Collection Coolie No.673 to say that he paid foreman
No. 72, Hai $ 30.00 to obtain a job as a monthly coolie. He was told
to say that this money was paid to 705 to give to Hai during March.
He further states that after a letter of complaint was sent by
their Union to the Commissioner of Police, they schooled him
in what he must say to the Police at Yulin Road Station (see
your report). He was further instructed to put his thumb impression
to confirm his statement. This man is very young and very frighten-
ed. They threatened to beat him up should he not comply with their
wishes and it appears very strongly to me that owing to his age
and timidity he was selected by the ring leaders to be the man
to do the dirty work. This Coolie begs of us not to let anyone
know of what he has reported. He definitely denies having paid
Hai any money at all as he said he got his job three years ago,
so why should he pay in March $ 30.00 to anyone.

I. R. Collection Coolie No. 647 Hsu Chi Ming age 44 years.
He states that he has served in the Eastern Division as a I. R.
Collection Coolie for 9 years. Has not any time paid any money
to Hai or Liu. He appears very scared and does not want to talk.
He certainly has been instructed to make false statements, but this
morning nothing could be got out of him.
Hsu Chi King is still very much alive.

（签名）

Subject Unrest among P.W.D. garbage removal coolies.

Made by D.S.I. Black. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At 9 a.m. 29-11-35 Mr. Vasilieff of the Antung Road P.W.D.
Depot came to the station and reported that he expected trouble
with his garbage removal coolies.
Enquiries show that there are about 80 coolies employed
at the Antung Road Depot. On the 28-11-35 Mr. Vasilieff had
occasion to dismiss two of these coolies, No. 646 for continuing
to dump refuse on waste land instead of the proper place. No.
705 for dumping on waste land and also employing a substitute
without first obtaining permission. (This substitute was senten-
ced to 20 days' detention on 26-11-35 for the larceny of tin
strips F.I.R. 1311/35).
At 5.45 a.m. 29-11-35 the coolies, headed by their apparent
ring-leader No. 673, approached Mr. Vasilieff and demanded
an explanation of the dismissal. After some bickering the coolies
went to do their normal duties, but intimated their intention
of returning at 2 p.m. to receive a reply to their query.
In view of the above 2 C.P.C.'s were posted at the depot
and D.S. White, D.S.I. Lee Yee Tong, C.J.S. 170, C.D.C's 218
and 232 attended at 2 p.m.
About 15 coolies headed by No. 573 arrived at 2 p.m. but
when it was explained to them by D.S. White through D.S.I. Lee
Yee Tong that the men had been dismissed through their breaking
the regulations, the whole party dispersed quickly.
During the conversations coolie No. 673 undertook the
part of spokesman.
There was no untoward incident observed.
C.P.C's and C.D.C's will be in appearance at 5.30 a.m.

先生，
1935年11月29日上午9时，工务处安东路堆栈的瓦西里耶夫先生（Mr. Vasilieff）来到巡捕房，报告称他预计其垃圾清运苦力会制造麻烦。
经查，安东路堆栈雇有约80名苦力。1935年11月28日，瓦西里耶夫先生借故解雇了其中两名苦力，第646号因继续将垃圾倾倒在荒地上而非指定地点；第705号因倾倒在荒地且未经事先许可雇佣替工。（该替工因盗窃铁皮条，于1935年11月26日被判处拘留20天，案件编号 F.I.R. 1311/35）。
1935年11月29日上午5时45分，由明显的头目第673号带领的苦力们接近瓦西里耶夫先生，要求解释解雇原因。经过一番争吵后，苦力们前去执行正常任务，但暗示他们将于下午2时回来听取对其询问的答复。
鉴于上述情况，两名中国巡长（C.P.C.'s）被部署在堆栈，副巡官 White、副督察长李义通（Lee Yee Tong）、华探长第170号、华探第218号和232号于下午2时到场。
约15名由第573号（原文如此，前文为673）带领的苦力于下午2时到达，但当副巡官 White 通过副督察长李义通向他们解释这些人因违反规定而被解雇时，全体人员迅速散去。
在谈话过程中，苦力第673号充当了发言人。
未观察到任何意外事件。
中国巡长和华探将于上午5时30分露面。

The 4th District Street Cleaners' Union held a meeting
on October 8 at 10 Ming Chi Li (鳴記里), Tung Yao Ka Jao,
off Whashing Road, U.O.L. Some 140 house refuse barrow
coolies attached to various P.W.D. depots in the Eastern
District attended. Chang Loong-hai (莊龍海), P.W.D. house
refuse barrow coolie No.673, who presided, stated that the
P.W.D. Authorities had decided to cancel the decision to deduct
$2 per mensem from coolies' wages as subscriptions towards the
cost of new barrows, and had refunded to the coolies the sums
already collected. In conclusion he stated that this
rescission of the order by the P.W.D. authorities was the result
of the firm attitude adopted by the Union, and urged those
present to canvass for new members. The meeting terminated
at 4.30 p.m.

Members of this Union, numbering about 150, recently
contributed $1 each to a fund raised to defray expenses.

It is reported that the promoters of this Union, named
Chang Dah Hai (莊大海), barrow coolie No.673, Wu Ning Fah
(胡銀发), Coolie No.641, and Li Ching Piao (李金標), ex-
foreman of the Cleansing Department, Eastern District, P.W.D.
are contemplating submitting the following demands to the
P.W.D. authorities :-
1) That the two clerks named Lur (樓) and Mei (梅) attached
to the Antung Road depot be either transferred or dismissed
for their oppressive attitude towards the coolies.
2) That all coolies be granted an increase in wages.

In compliance with a request from the
A/Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch), Lee King-piao
and Chao Teh-yu called at the offices of the Special Branch

收到报告称，受雇于工务局东区的某些生活垃圾清运独轮车苦力中的煽动者正准备组织工会，并且这些煽动者正采取强制措施迫使苦力每人捐款1.00美元以资助该运动。另据报道，居住在延山路207号的李金标（李金標），系工务局东区清洁部前领班，以及芝罘路315/317号“朱兴”面粉店店主曹德裕（曹德裕），是该运动的发起人之一，并得到两名苦力胡银福（胡銀福）（第641号）和庄大海（莊大海）（第673号）的协助。

应代理副警务处长（特科）的要求，李金标和曹德裕于1935年9月18日上午前往特科办公室。代理副警务处长就此事对他们进行了讯问，但他们否认知晓东区独轮车苦力中有任何组建工会的运动。他们还表示对这些人苦力的活动不感兴趣。在离开之前，代理副警务处长告诫他们不要参与任何与他们无关的事务，并告知将对这个非法团体的发起人采取严厉行动。
